name: De Quervain Tenosynovitis
summary: Painful disorder of the first dorsal extensor compartment involving abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis tendons.

looksLike: Pain with lifting, gripping or thumb movement
redFlags: Sudden tendon dysfunction or neurological deficit
firstSteps: Consider thumb-spica support for short-term symptom control
Maintain comfortable finger and wrist motion
selfCare: Use two hands or larger joints for heavy tasks where possible

assess: Grip or pinch may be limited
Radial wrist pain with thumb use
Rule out fracture or other wrist pathology

tests.name: Finkelstein Test
tests.purpose: Assess symptom reproduction at first dorsal compartment; perform gently to avoid false positives.
tests.positive: Familiar focal pain over radial styloid/first compartment.

stages.label: Protection, Education & Symptom-Guided Loading
stages.goal: Address safety, settle excessive irritability and maintain useful movement.
do: Consider thumb-spica support for short-term symptom control
Maintain comfortable finger and wrist motion
dose: Pain-free thumb/wrist ROM: 5–10 reps, several times/day
moveOn: Daily function is stable or improving.
No new red flags or progressive neurological deficit.
Exercise response returns to baseline by the following day.

stages.label: Mobility, Strength & Capacity
stages.goal: Restore the specific strength, mobility and control required by the condition.
when: Daily function is stable or improving.

Gradually restore lifting and pinch tasks
moveOn: Target movement and resistance are tolerated with good quality.

stages.label: Functional Restoration & Return to Activity
stages.goal: Rebuild real-world, occupational or sporting capacity.
when: Target movement and resistance are tolerated with good quality.
Functional capacity is improving without sustained symptom flare.
Progression is based on objective performance and patient goals.
do: Build sustained grip, pinch and lifting capacity
Return to repetitive work with graded volume
dose: Functional pinch/grip and lifting: 2–4 sets, graded load
Increase task duration in small increments
moveOn: Full task exposure is completed progressively.
No clinically meaningful deterioration during the following 24 hours.

returnCriteria: No significant symptom flare after daily activity

logic: Reduce the most provocative thumb/wrist load temporarily, then rebuild tendon capacity.
Splinting can be useful short term when daily tasks repeatedly irritate symptoms.
mechanism: Repeated thumb abduction/extension and wrist deviation
Sustained infant carrying, lifting or repetitive hand tasks may contribute
classification: Tendon-sheath irritation/stenosis; anatomical septation may affect response
investigations: Usually clinical; radiograph if trauma/fracture or thumb-base arthritis suspected.
Ultrasound may help when diagnosis is unclear or injection planning is considered.
manual: Gentle soft-tissue or wrist mobility may be adjunctive if restriction exists.
Avoid forceful friction over an irritable tendon sheath.
Gentle soft-tissue treatment to forearm/thumb tendons
Avoid aggressive friction in highly irritable tissue
Gentle forearm/thumb soft-tissue techniques for comfort.
Avoid aggressive friction over highly irritable tendon sheaths.
modalities: Thumb-spica splint can reduce provocative load; fit and duration should be individualised.
Corticosteroid injection is a medical option for selected patients; discuss risks/benefits with prescriber.
Short-term thumb-spica support may reduce aggravating load
Thumb-spica support may be used short term; heat/cold only for comfort.
dosing: Progress to isotonic thumb/wrist loading: 3 sets × 8–15 reps.
progression: Return gradually to repetitive work/caregiving tasks
Reduce splint use as load tolerance improves.
mistakes: Splinting without progressive return to loading
pearls: Pain location and task history are more useful than one provocative test.
Consider postpartum and caregiving load patterns without assuming causation.
education: Teach load modification rather than total rest.
Use larger joints/two hands for heavy tasks temporarily.
escalation: Medical review for persistent severe symptoms or consideration of injection/surgical options

tests.name: Finkelstein Test
tests.purpose: Assess symptom reproduction at first dorsal compartment; perform gently to avoid false positives.
tests.positive: Familiar focal pain over radial styloid/first compartment.
tests.patientPosition: Patient places thumb comfortably in palm; clinician gently ulnarly deviates wrist without forceful compression.
tests.therapistPosition: Position yourself to observe and stabilise the relevant segment without forcing the movement.
tests.handPlacement: Use comfortable, controlled contact appropriate to the test; avoid painful compression or excessive force.
procedure: Explain the test and obtain consent.
Screen contraindications and compare sides when appropriate.
Perform the movement slowly and apply only the required resistance or stress.
Record familiar symptom reproduction, range, strength and side-to-side difference.
tests.interpretation: Supports De Quervain pattern but is not diagnostic alone; distinguish thumb CMC arthritis and intersection syndrome.
tests.clinicalNote: A special test modifies clinical probability; it does not confirm a diagnosis in isolation.
